To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the matching-to-sample method of establishing stimulus classes can be used to extend sequence-class membership and that the production of novel sequences that were not explicitly trained suggests an empirical approach to analysis of the grammatical behavior of normal adults.
the matching-to-sample paradigm can be used to train stimulus class membership and that this training is sufficient for the production of simple sequences.
the matching to sample procedure can be used to establish classes of stimuli that are then used to control the sequential ordering of responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acquisition and development of stimulus control in humans.
the acquisition and transfer of simple sequential behavior, and with the role of stimulus-class membership in the production and reproduction of simple sequential behavior.
the development of procedures for the study of simple grammatical processes in normal children and retarded adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this experiment is a good example of the way in which a complex and difficult task can be broken down into a number of simpler components.
this experiment demonstrated the production of sequences that are not directly trained, and that this production was based on a matching-to-sample task.
the matching-to-sample paradigm can be used to extend stimulus-class membership to a set of novel stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present results support a stimulus-class approach to the study of sequential responding.
the matching-to-sample paradigm can serve to establish stimulus classes and that such classes can be used in the subsequent production of sequences.
matching to sample, when used to establish a stimulus class, can produce sequences that are predictable in terms of the stimulus-class memberships of the elements of the sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the matching-to-sample task is a useful procedure for establishing stimulus classes.
the matching-to-sample paradigm may be used to establish stimulus classes, which can in turn be used to produce novel sequences.
we can train a person to respond to stimuli in a sequence, then use matching to sample to extend sequence-class membership.
